summary: Rabbi Tawil examines the tragic events of Shemuel II Chapter 13, focusing on the violation of Tamar by her half-brother Amnon and the subsequent murder of Amnon by Avshalom. He discusses the family dynamics within the house of David, the psychological motivations of the characters, and the parallels between this narrative and the stories of Dina and Yosef. The class highlights the contrast between Amnon's lack of accountability and David's own approach to his past sins.
questions: Why were Amnon and Tamar not considered biological siblings?
What was the role of Yonadav in the plot against Tamar?
Why did David remain passive after hearing about the violation of his daughter?
How does the story of Amnon and Tamar compare to the story of Dina and Shechem?
What does the text reveal about the nature of desire and self-loathing?
